call: Which data is development and which is the sealed holdout
choice: Dev: EWARS monthly example + Nicaragua weekly before 2018; holdout: Laos monthly subset + Nicaragua weekly from 2018
alternatives: (a) The plan's default, holdout = one or two whole chap-core datasets with weekly development on the EWARS `example_data/`. Rejected: that weekly example has 8 periods, too short for a lagged backtest, so the weekly code path would first meet real data at the holdout. (b) A location split of the Nicaragua data. Rejected: chap backtests forecast every location jointly, and the iid spatial effect is fitted per location, so a location holdout tests a different thing from a time holdout. (c) Monthly holdout from `small_laos_data_with_polygons3.csv`. Rejected: its periods are weekly ranges, so it is not monthly.
basis: Chosen from file names, columns, row counts, location ids (no overlap with the monthly development locations) and period ranges only, before any values were looked at. The 2018 cut leaves 14 years of weekly history for development and about 5 years of held-out targets.

call: The chap backtest settings used for every R and Python evaluation
choice: n_periods 3, n_splits 7, stride 1 (chap eval's defaults); fixed in scripts/backtest_settings.env
alternatives: A longer horizon or more splits (e.g. 12 splits) for a tighter L5 estimate. Not chosen now: each split is one INLA fit under amd64 emulation, and the noise-floor runs of batch 4 multiply the cost; more splits can be added by a §4b entry if batch 5 finds the L5 comparison under-powered.
basis: chap's own defaults; n_periods equals the EWARS default prediction_periods (3), so the service is asked for its default horizon.

call: How chap-core is installed
choice: git clone at the pinned commit, then `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --python 3.13` from that commit's uv.lock
alternatives: (a) `uv tool install chap-core --python 3.13`, as chap's setup guide says. Rejected: it installs the latest PyPI release and resolves dependencies at install time, so the platform would drift from the pinned commit. (b) `uv tool install` from the pinned clone. Rejected: still re-resolves dependencies, ignoring the lockfile.
basis: The evaluation platform is an anchor and must be pinned (plan §4); chap-core ships a lockfile at that commit.

call: Which future-weather provider chap's backtest uses
choice: `climatology`, chap's default, passed explicitly: the covariates of each forecast window are forecast per location from month/week of year, not taken from the observations
alternatives: `observed` (chap's legacy provider): the model sees the true future rainfall and temperature, which isolates the model from weather-forecast error. Not chosen: chap names climatology as the setting that reflects production, it is what chap does unless told otherwise, and R and Python see the identical covariates either way, so the fidelity comparison does not depend on the choice. A candidate perturbation for phase D.
basis: chap_core/assessment/weather_providers/__init__.py (DEFAULT_WEATHER_PROVIDER_ID = 'climatology'); api_types.BacktestParams description.

call: What the model is given from the development files
choice: Each file reduced to the six-column chap data contract (time_period, rainfall, mean_temperature, disease_cases, population, location); rows and values copied exactly
alternatives: (a) The archived files as they are. Fails for monthly data (CH-07). (b) Drop only `month`. Rejected: the other derived columns (ID_year, E, Cases) are also used by predict.R when present and are also forecast by chap's weather provider for the future window, so they would reach the model altered too; dropping all of them is the same rule for every dataset. (c) Switch the weather provider to `observed` so the columns survive. Rejected: it changes the backtest, not the input (JC-04).
basis: The EWARS README's data contract lists the six columns, and says the derived columns are produced by predict.R's adapters, so 'callers do not need to supply them'. Diagnosis in results/diagnose_monthly/ shows the reduced monthly file runs.
matters: not yet tested; it is the condition for monthly scores existing at all

call: How the EWARS configuration is passed to chap
choice: A configuration YAML stating the EwarsConfig defaults explicitly (n_lags [3], precision 0.01, region_seasonal false, covariates rainfall + mean_temperature)
alternatives: No YAML, letting the service apply its own defaults. Equivalent in effect at this commit, but leaves the configuration implicit, and the batch-4 config variants need the YAML route anyway, where an omitted covariate list silently means none (CH-08).
basis: main.py EwarsConfig; chap_core/models/external_chapkit_model.py _chapkit_config_payload.

call: Which chap baselines are run
choice: chap-core's three built-in models with role `baseline`: global_median, seasonal_median, persistence (`builtin:<name>`)
alternatives: NaiveEstimator (`naive_model`, a Poisson draw around the per-location mean) and the scikit-learn Poisson regressors in chap_core/predictor/. Not run: chap's docs describe them as test stand-ins, not as baselines; the REST API runs exactly the three role-baseline models on every backtest.
basis: chap_core/models/builtin/*.py (role=ModelTemplateRole.baseline); docs/contributor/modeling_internals.md.

call: Which R reference image is run
choice: The CI-built GHCR image tag sha-964eea8, pinned by digest sha256:959fb4f0…c6ff88; the run checks that /api/v1/info reports git_revision 964eea8b…
alternatives: A local build from the pinned clone. Not needed: the plan asks for it only if the digest cannot be tied to the pinned commit, and the publish workflow's sha tag plus the reported git_revision tie it.
basis: Archive/chapkit_ewars_model/src/.github/workflows/publish-docker.yml (type=sha tags, GIT_REVISION build arg); results/run1/service_info.json.

call: What counts as 'every R call' in the inventory
choice: Every SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL R's parser finds in predict.R, lib.R and train.R, resolved with find() after loading the scripts' packages, plus the f() terms inside the formula strings; main.py has no R calls and is covered by the service design (batch 11)
alternatives: A reading of the scripts (incomplete by construction); a trace of the calls made at run time (would miss branches not taken, e.g. region_seasonal and the weekly path, unless every variant were run).
basis: results/r_calls.tsv: 171 call sites, 65 distinct; unmapped.txt empty.

call: Inference candidate (c): is there a credible existing Python INLA implementation?
choice: No candidate (c) as such. pyINLA rejected; pylgm noted as a possible building block for candidate (a), to decide in batch 8
alternatives: (i) pyINLA 0.1.11: rejected. It wraps the compiled `inla` program, the same engine R-INLA calls, so like rpy2 it is a way of calling INLA rather than a Python version of it (plan §4); its declared licence is 'Proprietary', incompatible with a public release of the tree; it ships no Python 3.13 wheel. (ii) pylgm 0.6.1 (MIT, from scratch, 878 tests): has an NB2 likelihood in INLA's parametrisation, offsets, iid, RW1 with sum-to-zero and Sørbye-Rue scaling, a Laplace fit and grid mixtures; lacks cyclic RW1, replicate, and the loggamma and pc.mgamma priors. Usable as candidate (c) only after extensions that amount to writing candidate (a).
basis: Archive/python-inla-candidates/ (PyPI metadata of both; pylgm sdist: likelihoods.py, effects/, priors.py, inference/). Found by web search 2026-10-14; a search can miss projects.
matters: decides how many inference candidates batches 8-10 build

call: Whether the Python port reproduces the R code's quirks or corrects them
choice: Reproduce them: the year shift computed from the last non-NA row of the whole frame, ISO week 53 folded by ((x-1) %% 52)+1, prediction of every NA-case row (historic ones included), NA cross-basis rows treated as 0
alternatives: Correct them (e.g. a 53-week cycle, predicting only the future window). Rejected for the main path: the aim is a Python version that gives results similar to the R original, and a correction is a different model whose differences would be confounded with translation error. A corrected variant is a candidate perturbation for phase D.
basis: Plan §1 (the model being translated is the one in predict.R/lib.R); CH-13, CH-16.

call: When and with what the main analysis environment is pinned
choice: Now, from the inventory: Python 3.13.0, numpy, scipy, pandas, pyyaml, dlnmpy @ 8c5edd79; the inference libraries added and the lock re-resolved when batches 8-10 build the candidates
alternatives: Pin everything now, guessing the inference libraries (NumPyro/JAX or PyMC). Rejected: a library guessed in advance is pinned for no reason (environment/README.md), and the choice between them is part of candidate (b)'s design. dlnmpy from PyPI 0.8.4 instead of the commit: the commit is the plan's pin; the two report the same version.
basis: environment/environment.yml, lock.txt; two-pass check passed (environment/README.md).

call: What every inference candidate must reproduce exactly, and what is candidate-specific
choice: Exactly, in every candidate: the likelihood (NB, mean E·exp(eta), size = exp(theta)), the priors (pc.mgamma(7) on log size; loggamma(1, 5e-05) on each log precision; N(0, 1e4) intercept; N(0, 1/precision) basis coefficients), the latent structures and their sum-to-zero constraints, and NA covariates as 0. Candidate-specific, and recorded per candidate: INLA's engine (strategy 'adaptive', int.strategy 'auto', the VB mean correction, compact mode, configuration-weighted sampling, skewness-corrected samples)
alternatives: Holding candidates to INLA's engine as well. Not possible for MCMC (candidate b) by design; for candidate (a) it is the target, met as far as feasible. The split makes an L3 difference attributable: the model is common, so a difference is the engine's.
basis: results/inla_defaults.tsv; Archive/r-sources/r-inla/src/rinla/R/posterior.sample.R; inlaprog/src/inla-priors.c.

call: What input the R reference harness fits, for the L1-L4 comparison
choice: Per development dataset, one window: the final 3 periods of every location are the future, with their observed covariates; the history and file shape are as chap hands the model (parent column, ISO weeks, location-major order, no disease_cases in the future)
alternatives: (a) chap's climatology covariates for the future, as in the backtest. Rejected: R and Python see identical inputs either way, and a weather model between data and fit adds nothing to a fidelity comparison. (b) Every backtest window. Rejected for cost; the chap repeats cover all 7 windows at L5.
basis: The weekly history equals, value for value, the historic.csv chap wrote into the R service's workspace for the same window (make_fit_inputs.py check).

call: How the R reference's posterior predictive draws are made reproducible
choice: set.seed(r_seed) before, and seed = inla_seed in, the one call inla.posterior.sample(s, model); nothing else in predict_chap is changed
alternatives: Leaving the sampler as the reference runs it (seed = 0: GMRFLib seeds itself at random, configurations drawn with R's RNG in parallel). Rejected: then no L4 draw can be reproduced. A non-zero seed forces the sampler serial (num.threads 1:1), which changes the random stream but not the distribution sampled.
basis: Archive/r-sources/r-inla/src/rinla/R/posterior.sample.R:452-567; qsample.R:20-27.
matters: untestable as intended: the fit the sampler draws from is not itself reproducible (CH-20)

call: How the archived predict.R is instrumented without modifying it
choice: predict.R is parsed and evaluated verbatim except its final CLI block (checked to be exactly `if (!interactive()) predict_chap(...)`); the instrumented function is built from predict_chap's parsed body by inserting tap calls between statements located by exact text and replacing the one sampler statement (JC-15). dlnm::crossbasis is shadowed by a wrapper that records the basis attributes and returns the result unchanged
alternatives: Copying predict_chap into the harness and editing the copy. Rejected: a copy can drift from the archive silently; insertion into the parsed archived body cannot, and instrumentation.txt lists every change.
basis: plan §3: the original is never modified; every copy-out recorded.
matters: no: the taps read values and change none (L1/L2 outputs identical across all 42 sweep fits)

call: How component seeds derive from the project seed
choice: seed(component) = 1 + (first 4 bytes of sha256('20261014/<component>'), big-endian) mod (2^31 - 2); components referenceHarness/repK/R and referenceHarness/repK/INLA; replicate K shares its seeds across datasets and variants
alternatives: A seed per dataset x variant x replicate. Rejected: shared streams make variant-to-variant L4 differences less noisy, and nothing requires independence. A counter-based derivation (project seed + K). Rejected: hashing names the component in the derivation, so a later node cannot collide by accident.
basis: provenance-record.md asks for per-component seeds derived from one project seed; this is the project's first stochastic node, so the rule is fixed here and stated in readme-at-start.md.

call: What of the harness's 168 MB of results goes into git
choice: Everything for replicate 1; for replicates 2-5 every summary, configuration table and predictions file; not their per-row frames, linear predictors, fitted values and posterior draws, nor any offset_check or rep1_repeat per-row file. The ignored files are listed with sha256 in results/fits_manifest.sha256 and regenerate from run.sh (up to CH-20)
alternatives: Committing all. Rejected: about 135 MB of compressed per-row CSVs, most of it identical in kind to replicate 1. Committing replicate 1 only. Rejected: batch 5 needs every replicate's predictions and summaries for the noise floor.
basis: plan §4 storage rule; .gitignore
matters: no; but because of CH-20 the ignored files do not regenerate bit for bit

call: How the L5 noise floor is sampled
choice: 4 unseeded chap evaluations of the R original per development dataset, exactly as batch 2's (same chap-core, image, inputs, config and backtest settings, read from node 01's files); EWARS only
alternatives: The plan's minimum of 2. Rejected: too few to see a spread. Re-running the baselines. Rejected: deterministic. Pooling with batch 2's run1 and tutorial run. Left to batch 5 to decide; they are the same evaluation.
basis: CH-10: the reference cannot be seeded through chap.

call: Where the Python model's code lives, and what the fidelity nodes test
choice: One package, the chapkit service folder analysis/05_pythonModel/scripts/chapkit_ewars_python/ (Q3's default, in the tree). Every node that checks the Python model at L1-L4 imports this package, so the code tested is the code chap runs; the service's lockfile pins the same numpy, scipy, pandas, pyyaml and dlnmpy versions as environment/lock.txt
alternatives: A copy of the model code per node. Rejected: the copies drift, and a test of one copy says nothing about the served one. A separate repository now. Rejected: Q3 defers that to the human
basis: The human asked for a runnable folder (plan §4b, 2026-10-17); one copy of the model code

call: The order of location labels behind as.integer(as.factor(ID_spat))
choice: Python's sorted() (code-point order)
alternatives: R's locale collation, which sorts case-insensitively under en_US. Not ported: it changes only which integer a location gets, the iid effect is exchangeable across locations, and on the development data both orders agree (L1 exact)
basis: results/l1_l2_comparison.tsv: ID_spat identical on every dataset and variant

call: The positions of the cyclic RW1 nodes
choice: Equally spaced: the port requires the distinct ID_time_cyclic values to be consecutive integers, and stops otherwise
alternatives: INLA's handling of irregular node positions. Not ported: months 1-12 and ISO weeks 1-52/53 are always consecutive in chap's data, and a gap would be a data error
basis: every development dataset and variant

call: How the sum-to-zero constraints of the cyclic RW1 terms are imposed
choice: Exactly, by writing each constrained block as x = T z with T an orthonormal basis of the sum-to-zero subspace; the model is an ordinary proper Gaussian in z. For the region-specific term, one constraint per location (per replicate)
alternatives: INLA's route: an unconstrained Gaussian corrected by conditioning on the constraint (kriging), with a matching determinant correction. The two give the same constrained Gaussian and the same theta-dependence of its normalising constant
basis: Python's Laplace log posterior at INLA's own 15 or 25 integration points equals INLA's to at most 2e-4 (weekly) and 0.016 (monthly) log units (03_inference)

call: Random numbers and seeding in the Python model
choice: numpy's default generator (PCG64). Without EWARS_SEED, the seed is derived from the project seed and the sha256 of the historic file, the future file and the config, so the same inputs give the same samples; EWARS_SEED overrides it
alternatives: Unseeded draws, as the R original makes (CH-10). Rejected: reproducibility (Rule 6) costs nothing here. Matching R's generator. Rejected: exact sample equality is not a goal (plan §3)
basis: plan §3; readme-at-start.md seed rule

call: How closeness between two runs is described at L3-L5
choice: L3: per posterior quantity, the shift in posterior mean in units of the pooled posterior sd, and the sd ratio. L4: per predicted row, the shift in predictive mean in pooled predictive sds, the ratio of 90 % interval widths, and the Wasserstein-1 distance between the 1000-sample sets in pooled sds. L5: chap's aggregate CRPS, and the paired per-row CRPS difference computed from chap's evaluation files (the per-row mean reproduces chap's crps exactly). No pass/fail
alternatives: Absolute differences (not comparable across quantities); KL divergence between Gaussian summaries (needs a distributional assumption the samples do not need); a tolerance file (dropped by the human)

call: Which R evaluations form the L5 run-to-run spread (left open by JC-19)
choice: Batch 2's run1 pooled with the chap repeats: 4 completed monthly evaluations plus 1 crash, 5 completed weekly ones
alternatives: The repeats only. Rejected: run1 is the same evaluation, by the same commands and pins
basis: JC-19

call: How the health of an R fit is labelled
choice: 'crashed': no predictions. 'flagged': a logged VB-correction abort, a non-zero mode status, or fewer than half the CCD design's integration points. 'clean': none of these. The labels describe; every fit is kept and every pair is reported with the labels of its two members
alternatives: Excluding flagged fits from the R spread (reading 2 of the batch 4 report). Not taken: the human chose reading 1
basis: plan §4b, 2026-10-17; the flags are those the batch 4 report named
matters: how the R spread is read

call: What of INLA's compact-mode engine candidate (a) reproduces, and where it departs
choice: Reproduced from the source (spec: 03_inference/a_laplaceCcd/results/inla_spec.md): the Laplace objective with INLA's prior normalisation and the 1e-4 RW1 diagonal; INLA's initial values; a central-difference Hessian with step sqrt(0.005) and a move to any better point it finds; theta(z) = theta* + V Lambda^-1/2 z; the skewness factors from z = +-sqrt(2) e_k normalised to product 1; the CCD design at radius 1.1 sqrt(m) with INLA's weights and the 6.9-log-unit drop; per configuration the VB correction of the mean with INLA's node set, 15-point Gauss-Hermite, step cap, stopping and abort rules; config sampling with probability proportional to density times weight; latent draws from the Gaussian approximation centred at the VB mean, theta[1] = exp(theta_k[1]). Departures: scipy's BFGS (gtol 1e-5) finds the mode instead of GMRFLib's 'smart' BFGS with its tolerances; the Hessian is taken along the coordinate axes instead of INLA's BFGS direction basis; the draw is centred at the VB mean projected orthogonally onto the constraint subspace instead of kriged in the Q metric; the Newton inner loop uses its own line search and a 1e-10 step tolerance; the likelihood derivatives are analytic instead of a 5-point stencil. The hyperparameter summaries in hyperpar.csv come from Monte Carlo (200 000 draws) of the split-normal approximation INLA's design is built on, not INLA's interpolated marginals
alternatives: Porting GMRFLib's BFGS (bfgs3.c, domin-interface.c). Not done: its path depends on GSL's line search, and INLA's own refits already move the mode by more than that path would explain (CH-20). Full MCMC: candidate (b), still open
basis: objective_at_inla_configs.tsv: the objective matches INLA's to <=2e-4 (weekly) and <=0.016 (monthly) log units; L3-L4 Python-vs-R inside the R-vs-R spread (06_closenessReport)
information: agent-retrieved (the spec was written by a subagent reading the archived C and R sources, with line citations)
matters: the mode search sets where the RW1 precision lands; see the theta-mode table

call: Scoring candidate (a) on the R-built design matrix as well as the Python one (plan §6, batches 8-10)
choice: Scored once, on the Python design matrix
alternatives: A second run on the R frame. Not run: the Python frame and cross-basis equal R's to 4.4e-16 on every dataset and variant (L1-L2), so the two runs would fit the same numbers
basis: 05_pythonModel/01_dataLayer/results/l1_l2_comparison.tsv

call: The Python service's image and runner
choice: chapkit's ShellModelRunner, as the original, running `python scripts/predict.py`; the image is python 3.13 with uv (ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.8.22-python3.13-bookworm-slim, pinned by digest), dependencies from the folder's uv.lock, no platform pin, so it runs natively on arm64 and amd64; id chapkit-ewars-model-python
alternatives: chapkit's in-process Python runner. Rejected: the original's runner type keeps the workspace layout and config handling identical. An amd64 pin like the original's. Rejected: nothing in the Python model needs it
basis: plan §6 batch 11: mirror the original main.py

call: Correction to the basis quoted in JC-23 and JC-28
choice: Over every clean R fit (not only replicate 1, which the earlier figure came from), the Python objective matches INLA's at INLA's integration points to at most 1e-4 log units (weekly) and 0.021 (monthly, no_covariates); JC-23 and JC-28 quoted 2e-4 and 0.016
basis: analysis/05_pythonModel/03_inference/a_laplaceCcd/results/objective_at_inla_configs.tsv; 06_closenessReport
